notes.title: The game is finally an actual metroidvania!
notes.content:
Ever since the beginning of development, I've been debating on whether or not to make the game linear or something more open like a metroidvania. Since the Red Sun is one of my first projects, I decided to start off with a linear game, since designing levels and gameplay would be much easier. However, I've always envisioned the game to be a metroidvania, where the player truely explores a ruined city where competing factions vie for power, and the environment adapts to the actions of the player. Today, I'm happy to announce that the very first steps of that vision have become real!

Players can finally explore the city in a way thats not just a straight line! Hopeful this means that it'll be more fun to go through the game, given to additional freedom of choice. As a part of converting the existing rooms into a walkable city, a bunch of new rooms and a couple mechanics were added, so even old players can still find new content while exploring. There also aren't any more rooms where all enemies have to be killed, so that should hopefully make the game easier, and help speed up the gameplay. There are even a couple skips that more speedrunning-inclined players can take! 

This updates basically represents the first iteration of my original vision. It took a lot of work and time just to get this basic version out, and its still missing a lot of critical components. Some of these are due to technical challenges (skill issue) and others are due to design challenges. Naturally, I plan on resolving these in the future. 

The most obvious of these is the lack of a map and a map system. Now of course this is a technical problem, but for me this is mostly a design problem. The current game world is a pretty horizontal city, and most if not all of the game takes place near or above the surface. This is done to reinforce the importance of the Red Sun, otherwise I'd probably make the some kind of layered city like an Sci-Fi Ecumenopolis or something like the setting of Arcane, with a nice shiny surface city, but a rough undercity (this sounds really cool in my head so I'm not throwing it out just yet). Instead, the current game map essentially consists of three horizontal layers, with connections between each layer, kind of like how Rain World does it. The reason that I mention Rainworld is because I hate the map system in that game (love the rest of it). It just doesn't make intuitive sense to me, and its hard to find you're way around while trying to piece together the different layers of the map. I think I can get around this problem by minimizing the number of layers showing the gameplay map, while also having a separate top down map of the city. Naturally, I have no idea how to do either yet, which is why it doesn't exist yet. 

Another problem comes from removing the linearity from the original demo. The linearity of the game allowed for some relatively unique set pieces and level designs, as well as preserve the feeling that the city is constantly changing (since I could just create a new scene that looked like the old room). I still want to preserve some of that linearity, while also showing that the player has a significant impact on the game world. In addition, I'm planning on adding some kind of faction system, where the strengths of each faction are kept track of, and affect the units found in gameplay. In order to preserve that feeling of finality, I decided not to respawn enemies like other metroidvanias (like say Hollow Knight). Instead, enemies that are killed will stay dead. This presents a pretty significant problem when it comes to backtracking, as frequently the player will enter reenter rooms, eventually killing all enemies and making traversal a boring chore (something thats pretty bad for a metroidvania). To counter this, I'm planning on introducing some kind of revival system, specifically for the robots, as it would make the most sense for them to come back to life. Specifically I'm thinking of adding some kind of resurrection robot, that goes around the game world reviving non-boss enemies. For the other factions, I'll probably add some kind of patrol mechanic, where factions send out small groups from their bases (another thing I'll need to implement).

Speaking of robots and factions, I need an actual story! Right now there's basically nothing, and the game heavily relies on environmental story telling. I don't even have real names for my enemies. For example, the circle polygons are called circle-dashers in the game code, while the enemy humans are named the spearman and (im not joking), the gun-spearman. Real creative stuff. In the next update, I really want to flesh out the world that players will be exploring. That means NPCs with actuals dialogue boxes, collectable items, and interactable objects. A part of this will be actually decorating the game world with more objects and set pieces, so that not every building looks exactly the same. Basically, I want to add some lore to the game so that theres an additional incentive to explore, instead of just "ooga booga smack more circles and squares", not that there's anything wrong with that. 

There's a bunch of other stuff missing, but for now I'm really happy with how the game is now, despite the many challenges I've brought converting the game into a metroidvania. I'm excited to add some more story elements, and finally start adding some of the factional interactions with the game world. 

TLDR: I converted the game to a metroidvania, but there's still a bunch of key features missing including a map, evolving ecosystem, and lore.

notes.title: Sorry for the delay! A big update is coming out!
notes.content:
Just wanted to make an announcement about the development of The Red Sun. Its been almost a month since the last build, so I wanted to explain what is going on. A big part of the delay between updates is that the Red Sun is being turned into a metroidvania! That was always a part of the plan, but I just kept making the game linear because it was a bit easier to do it that way. Converting to a true metroidvania takes design time and comes with a few small technical challenges, along with a lot more work than I expected. But its coming along nicely so hopefully a rough build will be out within a week or two. Conversion probably added a bunch of new bugs so keep that in mind. 

Thanks it! Bye.

notes.title: Changelog 0.88: Healing, Boss Changes, and QOL
notes.content:
I've avoided adding healing to the game, mostly because I was lazy, partly because I wasn't sure how it would affect the difficulty curve of the game. However, given the steep curve near the beginning of the game, I felt that a drastic change was needed. Healing should balance the difficulty. It works on the same system as the laser, where having 3 pips allows for healing. Having purple pips means that the player heals twice as fast (0.75s vs 1.5s). This should further incentivize aggressively evasive play by providing increased room for making mistakes. In game testing, players often manually respawn if they take damage early. Healing will hopefully mitigate this problem, as health is now a semi-renewable resource. 

Healing should not significantly affect boss battles, though it should make some significantly easier. Annie and Em & Be both provide opportunities for healing, which further aids new players fighting against the first two bosses. Steve also provided this opportunity, however, players were already too passive when fighting against Steve, and healing was likely to further encourage passive behavior. In order to counter this, Steve's movement speed was significantly increased, reducing the opportunities for healing, while also making it slightly easier for skilled players to deal damage, since Steve would be in range far more often. In addition, Steve no longer spawns more than 5 minions at a time, which would happen occasionally and be far to overwhelming to play against. 

A small change to Annie's AI reduces the change that Annie drifts downward when attacking from the side. 

By popular request, floaters no longer deal damage through walls, meaning that if there is a wall in between the player and the enemy, no damage will be dealt by floaters. However, if the enemy can still "see" the player, then the floater can deal damage. 

The saber sprite was updated, and the player sprite now has shoulder pads. Updating the saber sprite had the added benefit of extending the range of the saber. This may result in unwanted behavior (Specifically at the rooftop) and strategies, which will a be tweaked in further updates. 

Controller support is still in testing. Currently, the game register's controllers as some kind of keyboard extender. Pressing a button on a controller maps to a particular button on the keyboard.

notes.title: Changelog 0.87: Boss changes, Control compatibility
notes.content:
After significant game testing, I've noticed that the bosses are a bit unfair at this point. Most of them fly too high for player to hit consistently, and often "run away" from the player. This evasive behavior also encourages the play to fight evasively as well, which results in repetitive gameplay. Similar to the changes to Steve, I've lowered the float height of Em and Be, along with lowering the ceiling and raising the sun, in order to allow for tighter combat scenarios. Annie received a more significant change, and now adjusts height based on where the player is.

Due to popular demand, the controls are allowed to bind to mouse buttons. Additionally, the first attempts controller compatibility were made.

Controls are now bindable to mouse buttons

notes.title: Changelog 0.86: Bossrush and Laser Combo changes!
notes.content:
One of the major problems/complaints I saw in game testing was how punishing getting damaged felt when the player had a laser ready. The complete reset of the combo significantly slows down the tempo of a fight, and forces the player to act evasively/passively, when the laser was implemented to encourage aggressive behavior. Now, getting hit will simply reduce the combo pips by one, allowing the player to quickly bounce back from being damaged, and continue combat without much effort. 

Oh also, a boss rush was added, which can be unlocked after beating the demo. No balancing changes were made, this mode was mostly added to challenge the developer and test if fighting each boss in a row without healing was even possible (it is, my time is 2:56).

notes.title: First Announcement + The entire changelog up until this point!
notes.content:
Hi there! So the Red Sun has been in development intermittently for just under 7 months now, so some form of announcement is probably long due. The demo has been out for about 2 months and there have been a lot of updates that I haven't been announcing, mostly because I totally forgot I could. That being said, I want to post changelogs every time I make an update, which will hopefully be every few days until I feel that the demo is polished enough. In any case, that means that there are a lot of updates that I have not posted, I'm posting the entire changelog since development started on January 7th, 2023. 

Some of the dates might be off a bit, but they should be decent ballparks. I just find it interesting to see how this game shaped up to be what it is today and thought some of you guys might be interested. Honestly it's kind of crazy how many breaks I took during development, and I hope I can be more consistent in the future. Anyways, I have a pretty big update cooking up, so hopefully it won't take 2 months until I release it!
